method: Read existing 90 timing samples, generated C++ and runtime/compiler sources; no new NPU run or compiler invocation.

compiled_internal_sync_regression.core: standalone AIV, not a MIX task
compiled_internal_sync_regression.cause: Async tail reserves event 7 for MTE2->V, reducing available internal IDs from 8 to 7; allocation fallback removes a set and replaces its wait with PIPE_ALL.
compiled_internal_sync_regression.scope: Internal compute loop, not task-end barrier. Contribution in microseconds has not been measured.

submit_count_scope: Static call sites include conditional alternatives and do not count runtime task instances.

scheduler_regression.behavior: Marked gated consumers with WAIT fanins select pending cores whose running producer has the same ResourceShape. If none matches, requeue rather than retaining ordinary idle/pending pre-dispatch.
scheduler_regression.scope: Source demonstrates loss of ordinary early-dispatch eligibility for these cross-type WAIT edges. Runtime incidence and timing cost are not measured.

fixed_protocol_overhead: Wait callback lookup/branch in marked kernels, including no-handoff executions
Async tail event chain and completion waits
async_tail_kind state store/reset and control-line DCCI
Successor probe and matching; gated marked task argument vector prepared on AICPU
limits: No new mechanism trace for expanded CSA; successful handoffs and hidden Scalar time unknown
Do not assign the full 14.99 us regression to the added barrier or any single task
Small prefix values and binary size are not execution latency measurements
MIX Score and QK/PV remain outside the prototype; their contribution cannot be inferred from kernel counts
priorities: Avoid internal pipeline degradation from async tail event allocation
Preserve ordinary early dispatch when same-core handoff is unavailable
Reduce no-handoff protocol cost and then trace actual overlap without enabling the currently disabling swimlane mode
